questions.question: Engine belts should be:
questions.explanation: Check your engine belts for tightness and wear. Each belt needs a different amount of tightness. Learn what is right for your vehicle.

questions.question: Low ground clearance can cause problems when driving:
questions.explanation: Low ground clearance makes it hard to cross railroad crossings. Trailers with low clearance and long trailers pulled by single-axle tractors are especially difficult.

questions.question: After coupling is complete, there should be:

options.text: Three inches of space between the upper and lower fifth wheel.
No space between the upper and lower fifth wheel.
A moderate amount of space between the upper and lower fifth wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: No space between the upper and lower fifth wheel.
questions.explanation: When checking the coupling, make sure there is no space between the upper and lower fifth wheel. The locking jaws must be closed tightly around the kingpin.

questions.question: An open car window in cold weather may mean the driver is:

options.text: Using the heat in their vehicle.

questions.explanation: Watch for signs that a driver may be impaired. Drivers who have drunk alcohol, are tired, are using drugs, or are sick can be dangerous. A driver with their window open in cold weather may be impaired.

questions.question: When parking a double or triple vehicle:

options.text: You should back into your parking spot.
You should park on the roadway.
You should park where you can pull forward to leave.
You should ask people to move their vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should park where you can pull forward to leave.
questions.explanation: Park a double or triple where you can pull forward when leaving. Check the parking lot layout so you don't need a long, difficult exit.

questions.question: If you feel sleepy while driving, you should:

options.text: Keep driving to finish the trip.
Drive faster to get there sooner.
Pull off the road and take a nap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull off the road and take a nap.
questions.explanation: If you feel sleepy, stop driving and rest. Fighting tiredness is dangerous and causes crashes. Energy pills are not safe because they may keep you awake but won't make you more alert. When they wear off, you will be even more tired.

questions.question: If your engine catches fire, you should:

options.text: Turn off the engine right away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off the engine right away.
questions.explanation: Turn off the engine as fast as you can to stop the fire from spreading. Do not open the hood unless you have to.

questions.question: Which gas is dangerous if the exhaust system leaks?
questions.explanation: A leaking exhaust system can allow carbon monoxide, a poison, to enter the cab or sleeper.

questions.question: Steering wheel play should not be more than:
questions.explanation: More than 10 degrees of steering wheel play (about two inches of movement on a 20-inch wheel) makes steering difficult.

questions.question: An application pressure gauge shows:

options.text: How much air pressure is being applied to the brakes.
How much air pressure is available.
How much air pressure is needed to stop the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: How much air pressure is being applied to the brakes.
questions.explanation: An application pressure gauge shows how much air pressure is being applied to the brakes. It helps drivers see if their brakes are starting to fade.

questions.question: What does a shut-off valve do?

options.text: It is on the front of a trailer.
It is on the instrument panel.
It stops air from leaving the air brake system.

questions.correctAnswerText: It stops air from leaving the air brake system.
questions.explanation: Shut-off valves control air flow between trailers. The rear shut-off valve must stay closed. This keeps air from leaving the brake system.

questions.question: What shows how much air pressure is in your vehicle's air tanks?
questions.explanation: Vehicles with air brakes must have a supply pressure gauge. This gauge tells you how much air pressure is in each air tank.

questions.question: Why should you not use the trailer hand valve while driving?

options.text: It will disconnect from the vehicle.
It can cause the trailer to skid.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can cause the trailer to skid.
questions.explanation: Never use the trailer hand valve while driving. It can cause your trailer to skid.

questions.question: When should you adjust your mirrors?

options.text: When you are standing next to the vehicle.

questions.explanation: Check mirrors before you start driving. With a trailer, you can only adjust mirrors correctly when the trailer is straight.

questions.question: What must you do first to inspect slack adjusters on S-cam brakes?

options.text: Park on a hill and test the brakes.
Put on gloves and push in the slack adjusters.
Remove the drum and look inside.
Chock the wheels and disengage the parking brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Chock the wheels and disengage the parking brake.
questions.explanation: Park on level ground. Place wheel chocks and release the parking brake. Then pull each slack adjuster to check it. It should move less than one inch. If it moves more, it needs repair.

questions.question: What does the application pressure gauge show?

options.text: How much air pressure is being applied to the brakes.
The temperature of the air in the brake system.
The pressure from the air compressor.
How many times the brakes have been used.

questions.correctAnswerText: How much air pressure is being applied to the brakes.
questions.explanation: The application pressure gauge shows the air pressure being applied to the brakes. Not all air brake vehicles have this gauge.

questions.question: What happens when only the tractor has an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS)?

options.text: The brakes will not work as well.

questions.explanation: If only the tractor has ABS, the risk of jackknifing is lower. You should still be able to steer and control the vehicle. If only the trailer has ABS, the trailer is less likely to swing out.

questions.question: What is the maximum safe air leakage rate for a double combination vehicle in a static leakage test?
questions.explanation: In a static leakage test, a double combination vehicle should not lose more than 3 psi in one minute. If it does, something needs to be repaired and you should not drive the vehicle.

questions.question: What happens if a trailer is too high when coupling?

options.text: It will not make a difference.

questions.explanation: Check the trailer height before coupling. If the trailer is too low, it can be damaged. If the trailer is too high, it may not couple correctly.

questions.question: Starting in what year did all new trailers have to have ABS?
questions.explanation: All trailers and converter dollies made on or after March 1, 1998 must have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS).
